root_idea.summary: The root has two established semantic axes: physical leanness or emaciation, and restraining or withholding oneself from something desired.
root_idea.development: The physical axis extends from loss of fat and bodily leanness to thinness in objects, barren land, and related descriptions. The second axis develops into abstaining from food, preferring another's need, exercising forbearance, and turning away from someone or something.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural adjective is presented under its supported singular Classical Arabic citation form.

senses.definition: Lean, meagre, or emaciated through loss of flesh or fat.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the plural عِجَافٌ. In the supplied occurrences it describes the lean cattle in the account of Joseph's dream; the plural is used for masculine and feminine referents.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become lean, meagre, emaciated, or weak; to lose fatness or plumpness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to an animal, horse, or cattle, and also more generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To withhold or restrain oneself from desired food, especially so that another may have it or become satisfied.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction is عَجَفَ نَفْسَهُ عَنِ الطَّعَامِ or عَلَى فُلَانٍ; it denotes deliberate self-denial despite desire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To constrain oneself to forbear, endure another's conduct, or exercise patience toward someone, including in tending a sick person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional reflexive construction with عَلَى expresses patient restraint rather than physical leanness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To withdraw oneself from or turn away from a person or thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction عَجَفَ عَنْ فُلَانٍ has the sense of becoming aloof or turning away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To eat less than enough, or to transfer one's food to another before satisfying one's own hunger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage concerns dietary self-denial, including withholding food during drought or dearth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed on poor or bad food and thereby become lean or emaciated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a dietary-result usage of the Form II verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render a horse, beast, or other animal lean, emaciated, or weak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form IV verb is causative and takes the animal made lean as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a people, to have their cattle in a lean condition or to confine them because of harsh and straitened circumstances.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This usage describes the condition or treatment of livestock under hardship, not simply the direct causation of leanness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Being in a difficult, hard, or straitened condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V verbal noun describing hardship or severity of circumstances.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Leanness, meagreness, or emaciation; also the rough, thickened, lean condition of bones associated with it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes the physical condition or its visible effect on the bones.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having scant flesh or being thin in a face, gums, or lips.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an extended adjectival application to particular body parts, including a face with little flesh and thin lips or gums.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind or variety of dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal usage distinct from the adjective عِجَافٌ.
A noun usage distinct from the plural adjective in the Quranic form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Grain or grains that do not increase.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression حَبٌّ عِجَافٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for time or fortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal usage reported as a name of time or one's fortune.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thin or slender, applied to an arrowhead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural expression نِصَالٌ عِجَافٌ refers to arrowheads that are thin or slender.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land lacking fertility or vegetation, especially land not rained upon or affected by drought.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is applied to land described as barren or deprived of productive growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dry or tough from leanness, emaciation, or disease; also short, compact, or contracted in build.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective may be applied to a body or person, including as an epithet for an old woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rusty, unpolished sword, or one sullied by remaining long without polishing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized adjectival usage concerning a sword's neglected and tarnished condition.
